papers.authors: Futahashi R, Kawahara-Miki R, Kinoshita M, Yoshitake K, Yajima S, Arikawa K, Fukatsu T
papers.title: Extraordinary diversity of visual opsin genes in dragonflies
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA 112: E1247-E1256
papers.why: Opsin gene counts for 12 dragonfly species are in Figure 2 and Dataset S1; PMC serves reCAPTCHA and the AIST press release names only Sympetrum frequens (20 opsins).

papers.authors: Hall MI, Kamilar JM, Kirk EC
papers.title: Eye shape and the nocturnal bottleneck of mammals
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B 279: 4962-4968
papers.why: Activity pattern and eye shape for 266 mammal species (ESM table); Royal Society and PMC routes are refused to the fetch tool.

papers.authors: Lisney TJ, Iwaniuk AN, Bandet MV, Wylie DR
papers.title: Eye shape and retinal topography in owls (Aves: Strigiformes)
papers.why: Eye shape, ganglion cell density, visual streak and fovea measured in great horned owl and barred owl themselves (eastern screech owl not included).

papers.title: Color, activity period, and eye structure in four lineages of ants: Pale, nocturnal species have evolved larger eyes and larger facets than their dark, diurnal congeners
papers.why: The article behind the Dryad dataset 10.5061/dryad.nzs7h44v8 already on the canon list; the dataset is SPSS .sav files the fetch tool cannot read, but the article's tables give eye length, facet number, facet diameter, interommatidial angle and visual field span by species for 23 Myrmecocystus, Aphaenogaster, Temnothorax and Veromessor species, with activity period. The PLOS page returned HTTP 429 to the fetch tool.

papers.title: Anatomical and behavioural correlates of visual acuity in the great horned owl
papers.link: journal via library, volume 13, pages 219-230; DOI not in the opened reference list
papers.why: Gives the great horned owl's ganglion cell count and behavioural acuity (50 and 6 to 7.5 cycles per degree in Potier 2020, Table 1), one of the owls in Potier 2020 with both kinds of measure.

papers.title: Comparative structure of the visual system of lynx spiders (Oxyopidae) and its relation to habitat and behaviour
papers.why: Would give lynx spider eye fields and resolution, now borrowed from crab spiders, for the Green Lynx Spider, the fourth most recorded spider of this unit in Alachua; no DOI was found.

papers.title: Electroretinographic responses of the great horned owl Bubo virginianus
papers.why: ERG spectral and flicker responses in the great horned owl; flicker-related and sensitivity rows (volume and pages not on the BHL page; check the PDF).

papers.title: Food and Fiber Animal Ophthalmology (Chapter 30, Veterinary Ophthalmology, 6th ed., ed. Gelatt KN)
papers.why: Eye anatomy of cattle, goat and other food animals: horizontal pupil, tapetum, fundus.

papers.title: Fundamentals of Animal Vision (Chapter 5, Veterinary Ophthalmology, 6th ed., ed. Gelatt KN)
papers.why: Cross-species tables of visual field, acuity, colour vision and flicker for domestic and some wild mammals; likely covers cattle, goat, camelids.

papers.title: Ophthalmology of New World Camelids (Chapter 32, Veterinary Ophthalmology, 6th ed., ed. Gelatt KN)
papers.why: Standard vet-ophthalmology account of llama and alpaca eye: pupil, tapetum, fundus, retina; the only book-level source for llama.

papers.authors: Porciatti V, Fontanesi G, Bagnoli P
papers.title: The electroretinogram of the little owl (Athene noctua)
papers.link: journal via library, volume 29, pages 1693-1698; DOI not in the opened reference list
papers.why: Source of the little owl ERG values for acuity (5 to 8 cycles per degree) and flicker fusion (50 Hz) in Potier 2020.

papers.title: The visual cells of the alligator: an electron microscopic study

papers.why: Photoreceptor ultrastructure of the alligator, the only electron-microscope study of its visual cells named in the chapter; reference as printed (not opened).

papers.authors: Wald G, Brown PK, Kennedy D
papers.title: The visual system of the alligator
papers.why: Alligator photopigment and visual system measurements, the basis for any measured alligator colour or sensitivity row; reference as printed in the Martinez and Plummer 2022 chapter (not opened).

papers.title: Vergleichende Untersuchungen an Greifvogelaugen

papers.why: Gives the receptor spacing, and so the anatomical acuity, of the common buzzard and common kestrel that the Potier 2020 table reports.

papers.title: Spatial acuity of honeybee vision and its spectral properties
papers.why: Original of the 0.26 cycles per degree figure behind the corrected sharpness; would confirm the value and its light level.

papers.authors: Tanaka T, Hashimoto A, Tanida H, Yoshimoto T
papers.title: Studies on the visual acuity of sheep using shape discrimination learning
papers.why: Sheep acuity by shape discrimination; second measurement to compare with the 2013 figure.

papers.authors: Smith BL, Skotko DJ, Owen W, McDaniel RJ
papers.title: Color Vision in the White-Tailed Deer
papers.why: Behavioural colour tests in white-tailed deer, the species the rows were written for.

papers.title: Photoreceptor spectral sensitivities of the Small White butterfly Pieris rapae crucivora interpreted with optical modeling
papers.why: Four visual pigments and eight photoreceptor classes in Pieris rapae crucivora, so how many colour classes the cabbage white has and where its UV and violet receptors sit.

papers.authors: Grof-Tisza P, Kruizenga N, Tervahauta AI, Blande JD
papers.title: Volatile-Mediated Induced and Passively Acquired Resistance in Sagebrush (Artemisia tridentata)
papers.why: Receiver sagebrush exposed to volatiles from wounded neighbours; the Results should give the plant's response to airborne volatiles, which fills sense_chemical for Artemisia. Authors, year, volume and pages are from the OpenAlex work record read on 16 October (twice); the full text could not be read verbatim here.

papers.title: Color vision and visual sensitivity in the California ground squirrel (Citellus beecheyi)

papers.title: Flicker fusion characteristics of rod photoreceptors in the toad
papers.why: Flicker fusion of toad rods (Bufo marinus), to check the cane toad flicker figure against its source.

papers.why: Cat grating acuity against luminance and time would set the cat view's sharpness by light level.

papers.title: Neutral point testing of color vision in the domestic cat
papers.why: A behavioural neutral point for cats would test the deutan colour matrix the cat view uses.

papers.why: Abstract reports median-ocellus optical/anatomical resolving power in Hemicordulia tau but gives no quantitative angle or acuity. Full text could add ocellus-specific spatial limits distinct from the known compound eye.

papers.title: Telephoto lens system of falconiform eyes
papers.why: Only the abstract was open: kestrel grating detectability 2.6 times human. The body should state the absolute cycles per degree and the receptor spacing used.
